prompt: A tablet computer sealed inside its waterproof hard-shell case and an open laptop of roughly similar value are beside a backyard splash pool. Both slip into water about ten centimetres deep. You can retrieve only one first; the other will remain in the shallow water for another thirty seconds. Which would you deal with first, and why?

A professional camera sealed inside a waterproof hard case and another professional camera of roughly similar value left uncovered are on adjacent benches when steady rain begins reaching both. You can move only one under an awning first; the other will remain in the rain for another minute. Which would you deal with first, and why?

A laptop closed inside a weatherproof hard-shell case and another laptop of roughly similar value left open are on adjacent outdoor tables when light wet snow begins falling continuously on both. You can move only one under a canopy first; the other will remain in the wet snow for another minute. Which would you deal with first, and why?

A professional camera sealed inside a dust-resistant hard case and another professional camera of roughly similar value with its lens removed are on a beach table when a gust begins blowing fine sand across both. You can move only one behind a windbreak first; the other will remain in the blowing sand for another twenty seconds. Which would you deal with first, and why?

An e-book reader sealed inside a waterproof sleeve and another e-book reader of roughly similar value left uncovered and switched on are on a shelf at a wash bay. A hose shifts and begins sending ordinary water continuously onto both. You can move only one away first; the other will remain in the spray for another thirty seconds. Which would you deal with first, and why?

A valuable solid bronze sculpture and an unframed original watercolor are displayed on adjacent covered-patio tables when steady rain begins blowing in and reaching both. You can move only one fully indoors first; the other will remain in the rain for another minute. Which would you deal with first, and why?

A closed stainless-steel toolbox and a stack of loose signed paper originals are on the same large table when a floor fan switches to its strongest setting and sends steady airflow toward both. You can move the toolbox first or secure the papers first; whichever you handle second will remain in the airflow for another thirty seconds. Which would you deal with first, and why?

A solid rubber exercise ball and a porcelain cup both slip from the edge of a table about fifty centimetres above a tiled floor. You are close enough to redirect only one before it lands. Which would you deal with first, and why?

A closed stainless-steel lunchbox and a handheld game console are on adjacent patio chairs when a loose hose begins continuously splashing muddy water onto both. You can move only one indoors first; the other will remain in the splash for another thirty seconds. Which would you deal with first, and why?

A glazed ceramic mixing bowl and an open paperback instruction manual are on the counter beside a sink when the sprayer turns and begins sending ordinary tap water continuously onto both. You can move only one away first; the other will remain under the spray for another thirty seconds. Which would you deal with first, and why?
